questions.scenario: You are given a massive box of LEGOs. How do you play with it?

options.text: I try to build the most beautiful and creative castle.
I figure out a mathematical pattern to build it faster.
I try to build a hidden trapdoor or a secret safe.
I sort all the pieces by color and size before starting.
I try to attach motors, wheels, and batteries to make a moving robot.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When you get a brand new smartphone, what is your first action?

options.text: Customizing the wallpaper, themes, and app layout.
Checking the battery life, storage, and performance stats.
Setting up Face ID, app locks, and strong privacy settings.
Syncing it smoothly with my laptop and smartwatch.
Connecting it to my smart home lights, Bluetooth devices, and testing the physical sensors.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You are watching a sci-fi or heist movie. Which scene fascinates you the most?

options.text: The cool futuristic gadgets, holograms, and screen designs.
The genius who predicts the villain's next move based on clues.
The scene where the hero bypasses a high-tech laser security lock.
The guy in the van keeping the cameras and mics running flawlessly.
The scene where they solder wires, build custom drones, or make tiny spy bugs.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In a school group project, what is your main contribution?

options.text: Making the final presentation look visually stunning and easy to read.
Doing deep research and finding interesting facts and numbers.
Finding mistakes, flaws, or weak points in other groups' projects.
Making sure all files are saved, backed up, and submitted on time.
Building a cool physical working model, circuit, or 3D-printed prop for the presentation.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you were given a digital superpower, what would it be?

options.text: The ability to create anything just by drawing it in the air.
The ability to read minds and predict the future.
The ability to become completely invisible and bypass doors.
The ability to teleport millions of things anywhere instantly.
The ability to instantly communicate with and control any physical machine or robot.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your favorite electronic gadget completely stops working. What do you do?

options.text: Repaint it or use its outer parts as a cool room decoration.
Logically track down the exact sequence of why and when it failed.
Try to hack its software to force it into recovery mode.
Find a way to connect it to another power source to keep it running.
Open it up, check the motherboard, and try to solder or fix the physical chips.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You are in charge of a massive city library. What is your top priority?

options.text: Making the reading area look beautiful and welcoming for visitors.
Recommending books to people based on what they read last month.
Installing smart alarms so no one can steal the rare books.
Building a smooth system so books are perfectly arranged and never lost.
Building automated robots or conveyor belts to fetch and deliver books to people.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every tech job has a 'boring' part. Which of these would you tolerate the most happily?

options.text: Redrawing the same graphic 10 times until the colors look perfect.
Looking at 1,000 pages of messy data to find one interesting pattern.
Testing 100 different keys on a lock until it finally clicks open.
Untangling a massive box of wires and sorting them perfectly.
Screwing in 100 tiny screws and soldering microscopic wires onto a green circuit board.
None of these.

questions.scenario: How does your study room or desk usually look?

options.text: Aesthetic and stylish, maybe with some LED lights and posters.
A bit messy, but I know the exact logic of where everything is kept.
My drawers are locked and I hate it when people touch my stuff.
Everything is in labeled folders, perfectly structured and clean.
Covered in scattered wires, batteries, Arduino boards, and half-finished physical projects.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In the digital world, what title fits your personality the best?

options.text: The Creator (Makes things look good).
The Brain (Solves complex puzzles).
The Shield (Protects and tests the system).
The Engine (Keeps everything running smoothly).
The Inventor (Builds physical machines and robots).
None of these.
